searchText: Update: It turns out that neutering SELFDESTRUCT creates a security risk in at least one contract. Check out the analysis here, under PineCore: https://nbviewer.jupyter.org/github/adompeldorius/selfdestruct-analysis/blob/4647fef99e2aa0a2031b997f3166f07dfa68d7cb/analysis.ipynb ``` the possibility of a SELFDESTRUCT deleting many storage slots and then a contract being created at the same address and reading those same storage slots in a subsequent transaction ``` wait it's possible to redeploy a new contract and get a new address that's the same as the previously destructed one? ``` Allow selfdestructing a contract if it was created in the same transaction, and neuter SELFDESTRUCT in all other cases. ``` No more corner cases in EVM please Yes, if you make arrangements for it. I still think it's a good idea for us to explicitely list out the bad solutions as options even if they are known to be problematic, so that we can write down why they are problematic and not do them.
